_schema.subject: server/nudge_policy.py NudgePolicy (mirror: apps/watch/shared/.../NudgeStateMachine.kt)
_schema.description: Golden test vectors for the nudge/escalation policy. Each case constructs one fresh policy from `config`, then feeds `inputs` in order — one policy call per input step — and asserts `expected[i]` after step i. Language-neutral on purpose: plain field names, timestamps in seconds as floats, no enums beyond the string literals listed here. A Kotlin (watch) or TypeScript (phone) port must produce identical `expected` from identical `inputs`.

config.cooldown_s: float — seconds with no qualifying (>= current level) observation before the channel drops exactly ONE level; comparison is strict `elapsed > cooldown_s`, so an exact tie does NOT drop
config.channels: list of channel labels the policy runs, in emission order ("A" | "B"); the shipped watch default is ["A", "B"]
config.subscriptions: list of {vector, sensitivity, haptics, channel}. `vector` is one of "yelling" | "aggressive_tone" | "interrupting" | "airtime" | "hr_spike"; `sensitivity` scales the incoming level (`round_half_up(level * sensitivity)` clamped to 0..3 — half-up, NOT banker's rounding: 0.5 -> 1, 1.5 -> 2); `haptics: false` means the vector never nudges; `channel` is the lane the vector escalates

inputs.t: float seconds — the policy clock for this call (monotonic within a case)
inputs.events: list of {vector, level} observed in this call; `level` is the raw 0..3 vector level BEFORE sensitivity scaling. An empty list is a legitimate step (a quiet tick — this is what lets cooldown de-escalation fire). Optional `db_over_baseline` (float) on a `yelling` event is the raw loudness the watch's offline machine would have seen; it is informational for the server and is the DRIVING input for the Kotlin single-channel machine, which maps it to a level via >=14 -> 3, >=10 -> 2, >=6 -> 1, else 0 (must agree with `level` — the Python driver asserts this)

expected.nudges: list of {channel, level, vectors} emitted by THIS call, at most one per channel, in `config.channels` order. `vectors` is the sorted, de-duplicated list of vector names that produced the new (max) level on an escalation, and [] on a cooldown de-escalation
expected.levels: map channel -> current level after this call, for every channel in `config.channels`

applies_to.watch: cases the Kotlin NudgeStateMachine can run as-is: single channel "A", every subscription at sensitivity 1.0 with haptics on, and each step carrying at most ONE `yelling` event with `db_over_baseline`. For those, an empty `events` step is fed as db_over_baseline=0.0, and `onLocalLoudness` must return `nudges[0].level` when `nudges` is non-empty and null otherwise
applies_to.phone: the future TypeScript port — every case

cases.name: below_threshold_no_nudge
cases.description: Level-0 observations (loudness under the +6 dB first threshold) never emit and never move the channel off 0. Source: NudgeStateMachine thresholds / test_haptics_off_vector_never_nudges's 'nothing happens' shape.

cases.name: single_nudge_then_sustain_is_silent
cases.description: First qualifying observation emits once; a repeat at the same level refreshes the decay clock but does NOT re-emit. Source: test_no_event_when_level_unchanged.

cases.name: escalates_and_cools_down
cases.description: The Kotlin NudgeStateMachineTest.escalatesAndCoolsDown vector verbatim: escalate to 2, sustain (clock -> t=2), quiet within cooldown (10-2=8) holds, quiet at t=23 (23-2=21 > 20) drops one level.

cases.name: cooldown_is_strictly_greater_than
cases.description: Hysteresis edge: elapsed == cooldown_s is NOT enough to drop (21-1=20, not > 20); the very next tick past it is. This is the exact tie the Kotlin test comment warns about.

cases.name: sustained_observation_refreshes_clock
cases.description: The 'Critical 2' fix (test_sustained_qualifying_event / sustainedLoudnessRefreshesClock): a qualifying observation at the current level rebases the decay clock, so a quiet reading 21 s after the ORIGINAL escalation but only 7 s after the refresh must not drop.

cases.name: stepwise_deescalation_3_to_0
cases.description: De-escalation is one level per cooldown expiry, never a snap to 0, and each drop rebases the clock (22-1, 43-22, 64-43 are all 21 > 20). Source: test_stepwise_deescalation / stepwiseDeescalation2To1To0, extended to a full 3 -> 0 walk.

cases.name: lower_observation_never_snaps_down
cases.description: A weaker observation while hot (level 1 under a level-3 channel) does nothing before cooldown, drops exactly one level per expiry after it, and once the channel decays down to that observation's level it becomes a sustaining (clock-refreshing, silent) input. Source: test_two_vectors_multi_step, expressed on a single vector so the watch can run it too.

cases.name: full_decay_then_fresh_escalation
cases.description: Reset semantics: there is no explicit reset call — a channel that has decayed all the way to 0 is indistinguishable from a fresh policy (a new session gets a new policy instance). After the walk down, a new observation escalates and emits again, and its clock starts from that new escalation.

cases.name: channels_are_independent
cases.description: Two lanes escalate, sustain and decay on their own clocks: A (yelling) and B (hr_spike) both emit at t=1; only A is refreshed at t=10; at t=25 B (25-1=24 > 20) drops while A (25-10=15) holds. Source: test_channels_are_independent.

cases.name: haptics_off_vector_never_nudges
cases.description: A subscription with haptics off is invisible to the policy even at level 3. Source: test_haptics_off_vector_never_nudges.

cases.name: sensitivity_scales_with_half_up_rounding
cases.description: sensitivity 0.5: level 1 -> 0.5 -> rounds UP to 1 (banker's rounding would give 0 and no nudge); level 3 -> 1.5 -> 2. Source: test_sensitivity_scales_level + test_rounding_half_up.

cases.name: sensitivity_clamps_to_three
cases.description: Over-sensitive subscriptions saturate at level 3 (2 * 2.0 = 4 -> 3); a later raw 3 (-> 6 -> 3) is a sustain, not a new emission.

cases.name: two_vectors_one_channel_max_and_ties
cases.description: Several vectors on one lane: the lane takes the MAX scaled level and `vectors` names only the vector(s) that produced it — one name on a clear winner, both names (sorted) on a tie at the new level. A lower co-occurring vector is not listed. Source: test_two_vectors_multi_step's channel setup.

cases.name: single_channel_policy_ignores_other_lane
cases.description: A caller running only channel A (the phone's realtime path) never nudges on a subscription routed to B, and its `levels` map has no phantom B entry. This is the one behavioural knob Foundation A added; the default two-lane config is unchanged.
